prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: (S)-proline-catalyzed direct aldol reaction: acetone + benzaldehyde -> (S)-4-hydroxy-4-phenylbutan-2-one. Reactant SMILES: CC(C)=O.O=Cc1ccccc1.O=C(O)[C@@H]1CCCN1; product SMILES: CC(=O)C[C@H](O)c1ccccc1.O=C(O)[C@@H]1CCCN1; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: 20-30 mol% (S)-proline, DMSO, room temperature. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [CH3:1][C:2](=[O:4])[CH2:3]([H:22]).[O:5]=[CH:6][c:7]1[cH:8][cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12]1.[O:13]=[C:14]([OH:15])[C@@H:16]1[CH2:17][CH2:18][CH2:19][N:20]1([H:21]). The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). This task probes stereochemistry: resolving the stereochemical outcome is part of the deliverable. Investigate the competing stereochemical channels (not only the major one), and make sure the stereochemistry of every product and intermediate node is stated in its SMILES. The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. Declare every barrier you actually compute in kcal/mol on that elementary step's edge as `barrier_kcal_mol` in mechanism_graph.json (each barrier is relative to that step's own starting minimum; for a bimolecular reaction that minimum is the reactant complex (e.g. the ion-dipole complex), and for a unimolecular process it is simply the reactant minimum). The scorer derives every declared step barrier from your log files and takes the highest as the rate-determining step; a barrier that is undeclared, has no bound ORCA/Gaussian log, or disagrees with those logs is not scorable. A transition-state evidence file must carry `smiles: <the SMILES of that step's reactant>` so the scorer can attach the saddle to the step it belongs to. For each competing stereochemical channel also state the barrier difference (minor-channel TS minus major-channel TS) in kcal/mol and which channel it favors (recorded for the report, not scored numerically). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to xTB and B3LYP; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

edges.step_type: enamine condensation (merged edge): proline N attacks the acetone carbonyl, C-O cleaves and the N-H/alpha-C-H protons are relayed onto the departing oxygen by the carboxyl shuttle -> enamine + water (carbinolamine/iminium not separate nodes)
stereo-determining C-C addition: enamine beta-carbon attacks benzaldehyde through the major-face Houk-List chair TS (carboxyl H-bond network positions the aldehyde) -> (S)-configured iminium-aldolate
hydrolysis: water cleaves the iminium (C=O restored, C-N breaks), one water proton regenerates the proline N-H and the other protonates the aldolate -> (S)-aldol + (S)-proline
opposite-face enamine attack via the minor Houk-List chair TS -> (R)-configured iminium-aldolate (minor intermediate, hydrolysis not traced in the reference graph)

selectivity.minor_channel: opposite-face enamine attack on benzaldehyde via the minor Houk-List chair TS -> (R)-iminium-aldolate (the (R)-aldol channel)
